articles.title: Z+ (abopflichtiger Inhalt); Landwirtschaft: Laborfleisch vom Bauernhof
articles.teaser: Statt Tieren will ein niederländischer Landwirt auf seinem Hof Fleisch aus Zellen züchten. Und das soll funktionieren? Unsere Autorin hat den Hof besucht.
articles.image_title:
Landwirtschaft: BU Vorschlag: Der Landwirt und Käsehersteller Corné van Leeuwen überprüft am 8. Dezember 2025 den Bioreaktor in der kleinen Produktionsstätte von RespectFarms auf dem Bauernhof von Corné van Leeuwen in Schipluiden, Niederlande. ++++++++++
SCHIPLUIDEN, THE NETHERLANDS - 8TH OF DECEMBER, 2025: Farmer and cheesemaker Corné van Leeuwen checks in the bioreactor at the small-scale production space and the future experience center of RespectFarms, at the farm of Corné van Leeuwen, in Schipluiden, the Netherlands, on the 8th of December, 2025. The farm is seen on the background. The production space and experience center are not running yet. Schipluiden has the world’s first cultivated meat farm, which is now being developed. At this farm agriculture and advanced biotechnology will in the future come together on the working farm of dairy farmer and cheesemaker Corné van Leeuwen. Alongside his traditional milk and cheese production, meat will be grown directly from animal cells in bioreactors, eliminating the need to raise and slaughter animals while keeping farmers at the center of food production. The project is led by RespectFarms, co-founded by Florentine Zieglowski, and supported by the Province of South Holland as a model for modernizing food systems without pushing farmers aside. Cultivated meat uses far less land and water and produces significantly fewer greenhouse gas emissions than conventional meat, while also improving animal welfare. For farmers, it offers a new and complementary source of income rooted in their existing knowledge and infrastructure. The farm includes a, not yet running, small-scale production space and future experience center where farmers, students, schools, and visitors in the future can learn about the technology. The focus is on testing, learning, and sharing knowledge rather than mass production. From 2026, trials with bioreactors of 20 to 200 liters will begin, leading to a fully operational pilot farm by 2028. The province is investing €500,000 to support knowledge exchange, outreach, and public engagement. As global demand for meat continues to rise, this initiative shows how innovation can reduce environmental pressure while strengthening rural economies. CREDIT: Ilvy Njiokiktjien
